newsitem.title: USA: American Electric Power could do more deals.
newsitem.headline: American Electric Power could do more deals.

text.p: American Electric Power Co Inc could still make further acquisitions after its proposed joint purchase, with Public Service Co of Colorado, of a British electric company moves forward, analysts said Monday.

"Given that American Electric Power had the resources to consummate a transaction like this (by itself), ... this may be a prelude to another, possibly more dilutive transaction for AEP, possibly a larger transaction," Smith Barney analyst William Tilles said.

Wheat First Butcher Singer analyst Thomas Hamlin agreed that structuring the deal with a partner keeps the door open for further AEP acquisitions. He said, "Yes, it frees up some equity for AEP to do some other foreign deals."

AEP spokesman Thomas Holliday, in a telephone interview, said no other deals were currently anticipated but added the company has entertained "various possibilities." Both companies, as reported, said they had considered other possible targets in the UK and elsewhere.
"Clearly, we are looking at various things across the board and internationally," Holliday said.

Columbus, Ohio-based AEP and Public Service of Colorado agreed to jointly acquire Britain's Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc, the latest in a series of such acquisitions by U.S. utility companies in Britain. The U.S. companies said the deal will be immediately accretive for both.

Yorkshire said it will not contest the $15.02 (927 pence) bid which at the time it was announced was valued at $2.43 billion or 1.5 billion pounds sterling. Yorkshire closed at 818.5 pence Friday and rose as high as 885 Monday.
AEP was up 1/4 at 42-1/8 and Public Service-Colorado was up 1 to 39-7/8, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said expanding overseas, particularly in Britain where utilities are further deregulated, gives U.S. firms experience operating in a more competitive environment.

David Schanzer, a Janney Montgomery Scott analyst, said that in light of the coming restructuring of the U.S. utility industry and of increasing competition, it is beneficial for U.S. companies to expand overseas and explore other options.
"The better companies in the United States tend to recognize the opportunities overseas," he said.
Smith Barney's Tilles said overseas moves are not crucial to U.S. firms but he said the deal makes sense financially.

Tilles kept a neutral rating on both but raised his 1997 earnings estimates for AEP to $3.35 a share from $3.30 versus $3.14 in 1996 and for Public Service- Colorado to $3.15 from $3.05 versus last year's $2.78 a share.
Public Service-Colorado had 1996 operating revenues of $2.17 billion while AEP revenues were $5.85 billion.
Analysts said they do not expect roadblocks from British regulators and said the deal is a positive for the U.S. firms.

"I think it's generally positive," said Legg Mason Wood Walker analyst Ronald Tanner. "We don't get real excited about these (British) acquisitions but in general they do well... It's not like hitting a home run but it's a single."
Linda Byus, an analyst at Nesbitt Burns Securities, said the deal seems to fit AEP's strategy.

In addition to its electricity business, Yorkshire owns a 22.5 percent stake in a British telecommunications firm, Ionica. In October, AEP formed a new subsidiary called AEP Communications. Some power companies are exploring telecommunications opportunities such as incorporating fiber optic lines on existing property rights of way.
A Public Service-Colorado merger with Southwestern Public Service Co is pending.
